pages.title: Sent Away
pages.text: My father has a name, an estate and a wife. I am the son of none of the three that matter. They were polite about it for years, which is how my family is cruel.$(br2)Then someone at court noticed that I could count, and my family was asked to keep me somewhere far.

pages.title: The Land
pages.text: They gave me this land. It is on the maps as a holding. In truth nothing had grown here in a generation, and they knew it. A gift one can neither refuse nor use is the family's favourite kind.$(br2)I arrived with a cart, a ledger and no staff.

pages.title: The Hut
pages.text: There was a hut. Someone had lived in it, long ago, and had left in no hurry. I never learned who.$(br2)The things on its walls were carved, not forged, and cut with marks I cannot read. I took what I could use and kept the rest tidy. It was not mine to throw out.

pages.title: The Soil
pages.text: The soil is not dead. It is tired, like a field after a bad lord. Whatever was wrong with it has been lifted already, by whom I cannot say, and nobody came back to notice.$(br2)So that is my posting. I am to make a dying land pay. I intend to.

pages.title: How to Read It
pages.text: This is a ledger, and I keep it as one. What I built, what it cost, what it returned.$(br2)Where I write a number, I counted it. Where I write that I do not know, I do not.
